title: Reading the game's own objectives
target: How missions, tasks and achievements are put together in Supermarket Simulator, so the objective you are working on is a structure you can read.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)

steps.do: Expect objectives to be run by a system and held in a container.
steps.because: missions run through a system of their own and are held in a container (MissionSystem, MissionContainer)

steps.do: Read a mission as a set of tasks rather than one instruction.
steps.because: a mission is built out of tasks of its own (Mission, MissionTask)

steps.do: Break order work into its three tasks.
steps.because: order work is three named tasks: filling, closing and delivering (FillOrderTask, CloseOrderTask, DeliverOrderTask)

steps.do: Look for the task that belongs to the scale.
steps.because: the scale has an interaction task of its own (ScaleInteractionTask)

steps.do: Read the type of a mission before deciding what it wants.
steps.because: a mission carries a type of its own (MissionType)

steps.do: Expect one kind of mission to be measured in steps rather than finished at once.
steps.because: one kind of mission is built around steps (ScaleStepMission)

steps.do: Know that a mission can be what switches a feature on.
steps.because: there is a mission that activates online orders (OnlineOrderActivateMission)

steps.do: Keep achievements apart from missions, because they are counted separately per platform.
steps.because: achievements are held in a container of their own and handled separately for the platforms the game ships on (AchievementContainer, SteamAchievements, XBoxAchievements)

commonMistakes: Treating a mission as a single instruction when it is a set of tasks.
Looking for order progress in one place rather than in filling, closing and delivering.
Assuming a step-based objective finishes the moment you start it.
Counting an achievement as a mission because they were earned together.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
